title: C475 — High mounted stoplamp connector
introduction:
The high mounted stoplamp has a simple message for following traffic; its connector sheet deserves equally clear reading. I start with the identification table, match the harness heading and drawing, then use the cavity labels to follow the control-module circuit and ground-return descriptions across their rows.

This reference identifies connections and service-parts entries. It does not teach access, connector release, physical probing direction, electrical testing or replacement. The gauge convention and Box, Size and Used codes are undefined here. Keep circuit-wire entries and pigtail entries in their own tables rather than treating them as interchangeable specifications.

edits.why: The printed drawing shows vertically stacked cavity labels within a rectangular face, with a rounded structure on the left and projecting features above and below. I use that asymmetry to recognize the illustration before reading its labels. It helps navigate the reference without establishing an installed orientation, release direction or access route.

Follow each cavity row across the circuit identifier, wire-color code, gauge entry, function and terminal reference. The functions distinguish the stoplamp control-module circuit from the ground return. Keep each terminal reference attached to its own row; the entries are not a blanket specification for the connector. The named ground area describes the circuit reference without showing the exact attachment point or proving continuity.

The kit entry leads from the identification table to the service-parts row. That row separates the service identifier, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity information. I keep it beside the original circuit table as a distinct reference: a service-pigtail gauge entry alone cannot resolve how to join it to the circuit wiring. The catalog image filename supplies no repair or installation instructions.
